extracted.intended_audience: sovereigns, legislators, rulers, and students of political theory
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for the sovereign representative about the duties, hazards, and administrative standards required to preserve the commonwealth (laws, instruction, taxation, justice, punishments, rewards, counsel, and crisis conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dual sovereign/master (civil vs ghostly)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Civill Power and the Ghostly Power both claim to declare what is Law, every Subject must obey two Masters, which is impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both powers oppose one another the commonwealth is in danger of civil war and dissolution; either the ghostly must be subordinate to the temporal or there is no supremacy but the temporal. The spiritual, though obscure, commands a party through fears of ghosts and punishments and can disturb or destroy the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent spiritual power from rivaling temporal sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: Either the Civill must be subordinate to the Ghostly, or the Ghostly must be subordinate to the Temporall; otherwise there is no Supremacy but the Temporall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign must ensure that essential rights of sovereignty are not undermined by spiritual authorities that command obedience by terror of punishments and rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixed government that creates multiple 'souls'
rubrics_metrics.description: When powers of levying money, conduct/command, and making laws are vested in distinct bodies, the commonwealth is effectively divided into three independent factions rather than one government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such division endangers consent to good laws and nourishment necessary for life and motion; a single representative person (sovereign) is required for unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reliable means of raising money
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulty of raising money for necessary uses—especially before war—threatens the commonwealth because subjects' opinion of proprietary rights obstructs passage of money to the public treasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign must preserve the right to levy money; when obstructed he may be forced to use laws or, as last resort, violent measures to obtain supplies. Repeated extremities either correct the people's contumacy or lead to ruin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent monopolies and abuses of public revenue (publicans)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the treasure of the commonwealth is gathered into excess in one or few private hands by monopolies or farms of public revenues, the state suffers an inflammation like pleurisy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against concentration of public wealth via monopolies or farmed revenues that produce systemic harm and feverish instability in the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control popularity of powerful subjects (popular men)
rubrics_metrics.description: The popularity of a potent subject can draw the people away from obedience to the laws toward following a man of unknown designs, producing rebellion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign must be cautious of flattering popular figures and prevent them from gaining influence that could challenge the sovereign; popularity in a popular government is especially dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit immoderate growth of towns and multitude of corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive greatness of a town able to field a large army, and a great number of corporations (many lesser commonwealths within a greater) are an infirmity to the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent internal concentrations of power that can act like independent bodies within the polity (compared to 'worms in the entrails' of a natural man).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress liberty to dispute against absolute sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberty of disputing against absolute power by pretenders to political prudence perpetually meddles with fundamental laws to the molestation of the commonwealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit or correct the spread of false doctrines and disputations that encourage subjects to judge laws by private opinion rather than by sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid insatiable appetite for enlarging dominion and ununited conquests
rubrics_metrics.description: An insatiable appetite for enlarging dominion (bulimia) and the wounds of ununited conquests are frequently a burden and sometimes are more easily lost than kept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereign should weigh costs of expansion; ununited conquests can be a drain and source of vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize dissolution condition (final defeat in war)
rubrics_metrics.description: If in war the enemies obtain a final victory such that the commonwealth's forces keep the field no longer, the commonwealth is dissolved and every man is at liberty to protect himself by his own discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sovereign power expires (practical protection gone), subjects' obligations may cease; sovereigns must avoid conditions that lead to final defeat, since assembly and sovereign rights perish with suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary office: procuration of the safety and contentments of the people
rubrics_metrics.description: The office of the sovereign consists in procuration of the safety of the people, not merely bare preservation but also all other contentments of life which every man by lawful industry without danger shall acquire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereign is obliged by natural law and accountable to God; obligation is to secure both protection and lawful means for people to obtain life's contentments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public instruction and laws rather than individualized caretaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign should secure people's welfare through public instruction (doctrine and example) and making/executing good laws rather than by care applied to individuals beyond protection from injuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and laws should be designed to let individuals apply general rules to their cases rather than rely on ad hoc sovereign interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not relinquish essential rights of sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: If the essential rights of sovereignty are taken away the commonwealth is dissolved; it is against the duty of the sovereign to transfer or lay aside any of these essential rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential rights include supreme judicature, making war and peace, judging necessities, levying money and soldiers, making officers, appointing teachers and examining doctrines; abandoning means abandons ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach the grounds and reasons of sovereign rights to the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign must not let the people be ignorant or misinformed of the grounds and reasons of his essential rights because ignorance makes men easy to seduce and resist when use is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds need diligent and true teaching; civil law alone cannot sustain obedience—natural law and instruction are necessary so people understand obligations beyond fear of punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach people not to desire change of government
rubrics_metrics.description: People are to be taught not to be in love with forms of government they see elsewhere nor to desire change; prosperity arises from obedience and concord, not the mere form of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that removing obedience destroys the commonwealth and reforms by disobedience risk destroying the state, illustrated by fable of daughters of Peleus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach people not to adhere to popular men or substitute them for sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: People should not be led by admiration of a fellow subject or assembly so as to defer obedience or honour appropriate only to the sovereign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn against influence from popular men whose flattery can seduce people from loyalty; sovereign authority must remain the source of conveyed influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach people not to dispute or speak evil of the sovereign representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects ought not to speak evil of the sovereign representative, argue and dispute his power, or use his name irreverently, actions which bring the sovereign into contempt and slacken obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear that irreverent speech undermines the obedience which is the safety of the commonwealth and should be discouraged by instruction and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set times and assemblies to instruct the people
rubrics_metrics.description: People cannot be taught and retain knowledge without setting apart times wherein they may attend those appointed to instruct them; such times should be determined for assembly and instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public solemnities (like Sabbath) to read and expound laws and duties, reminding people where sovereign power lies and reinforcing civic education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach children honour to parents (familial deference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Children should be obedient to parents while under their tuition and show honour afterwards; originally the father was also his sovereign lord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should include that fathers retained honour in recognition for education; this encourages social order and relates to the fifth commandment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach prevention of injury and the principles of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign ought to cause justice to be taught: abstain from violence, violation of conjugal honour, rapine, and fraudulent surreption of one another's goods; show the evils of false judgment by corrupt judges or witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice consists in taking from no man what is his; offences against private persons cannot be pardoned without consent or reasonable satisfaction; justice must be equally administred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach that unjust designs and intentions are themselves injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only unjust facts but the designs and intentions to do them (though hindered) are injustice—pravity of the will counts as injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral instruction should inculcate that internal intention matters (tenth commandment as summary of second table: mutual charity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use universities and schools to instruct youth correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction of the people depends wholly on right teaching of youth in the universities; false doctrines are perpetuated by poor teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereign should ensure universities teach doctrines that uphold civil authority and not those that uphold papal or other external powers; reform of universities may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure equal administration of justice (equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice must be equally administered to all degrees of people so the rich and mighty as well as the poor and obscure may be righted of injuries; partiality aggravates offences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality of justice is a precept of natural law and sovereign is as subject to it as any; impunity breeds insolence, hatred, and endeavours to pull down oppressing greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose equal taxes according to equal debt for defence
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality of imposition depends not on equality of riches but on equality of the debt every man owes to the commonwealth for his defence—the impositions are wages due to those who hold the public sword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxation should be levied on consumption/use rather than mere riches so each pays equally for the benefit of defense; taxing consumption avoids defrauding the commonwealth by luxury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public charity for those unable to maintain themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who by unavoidable accident become unable to maintain themselves ought to be provided for by the laws of the commonwealth rather than left to private charity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State provision is required as an obligation of the sovereign; leaving incapacitated people to uncertain private charity is uncharitable in a sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent idleness: force the able-bodied to work and encourage arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Able-bodied idle people should be forced to work; there ought to be laws encouraging arts (navigation, agriculture, fishing, manufacture) and transplantation of populations to less inhabited countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide employment through encouragement of arts and colonization; when the world is overcharged with inhabitants the last remedy is war (victory or death)—implying the sovereign must manage population and labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make good laws: necessary and perspicuous
rubrics_metrics.description: A good law is that which is needful for the good of the people and withal perspicuous; unnecessary laws are traps for money and multiply ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws should be as short and as proper and significant as possible; perspicuity comes from declaring the causes and motives for which the law was made, not from prolixity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply punishments rightly: correction not revenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The end of punishing is correction of offender or others by his example, not revenge; severest punishments for crimes most dangerous to the public (contempt of government, corruption of justice, provoking public indignation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use severity for crimes that threaten the public; exercise lenity for crimes of infirmity (provocation, fear, ignorance) where possible. Punish leaders and teachers, not seduced poor people, to avoid harming the commonwealth and to account for sovereign's instructional faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply rewards to encourage genuine service, not to buy off ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewards should be applied so that those who have served the commonwealth are recompensed with as little expense as possible and in ways that encourage others to serve; buying off popular ambitious subjects is counterproductive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rewarding ambition that disturbs the peace (which breeds more ambition); rewards should incentivize service and skill rather than pacify troublemakers for short-term quiet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose counsellors with least self-interest and most public knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign should choose counsellors who have least hope of benefit by giving evil counsel and most knowledge of matters conducive to peace and defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of counsellors who soothe people over unreasonable grievances for private advantage; prefer those disinterested in public troubles and experienced in public affairs.
